en: 🇺🇸 2001: collapse within ten years. 2011: still standing. So… let’s reschedule for 2012. 😅

zh: 📅 2011年到了，中国没按剧本谢幕。
en: 2011 arrived. China forgot to follow the script. 🎬

zh: “预测错了”是第一集；“但我还是不撤回”是第二集。
en: “I was wrong” was episode one; “but I’m not retracting it” was episode two. 🍿

zh: 2026：这日历是不是需要升级一下？
en: 2001: collapse in 2011. 2011: collapse in 2012.

zh: 2026: Maybe the calendar needs an update? 📅
en: 预测最大的敌人不是反对者，是时间。

zh: The biggest enemy of a prediction isn't criticism. It's time. ⏰
en: WTO入世曾被视为“崩溃倒计时”的重要节点，结果中国并没有按这个剧本走。

zh: WTO accession was treated as a major countdown trigger. China didn't follow that script. 📉➡️📈
en: 2001年的倒计时，时间走完了；倒计时对象还在。

zh: The 2001 countdown reached zero. The subject of the countdown didn't. ⏱️
en: 十年预测，准点到期；现实世界拒绝兑付。

zh: The ten-year forecast expired on schedule. Reality declined to redeem it. 😶
en: “还有一年”在预测学里可能叫延期，在互联网里通常叫续杯。

zh: “One more year” may be called a revision in forecasting; online, we call it a refill. ☕😂
en: 2011没发生，于是2012继续等。

zh: 2011 didn't happen, so 2012 got the sequel. 🎬
en: 这不是预测系列，这是《明年一定崩》的长篇连载。

zh: This isn't a prediction series; it's an ongoing “collapse next year” saga. 📚
en: 2001年的书名叫《The Coming Collapse of China》。关键词是“Coming”。

zh: The 2001 book was called The Coming Collapse of China. The key word is “coming.” 🚂
en: 问题来了：Coming到底是现在进行时，还是永远将来时？

zh: The question is: Is “coming” present progressive—or eternal future tense? 🤔
en: 预测可以错一次；问题是这一次后来又被重新排期了。

zh: A prediction can be wrong once. The interesting part is when the deadline gets rescheduled. 📆
en: 2011年的“崩溃”没有出现，2012年的版本也没有出现。

zh: The 2011 collapse didn't arrive. Neither did the 2012 edition. 🚫
en: 书名没变，截止日期倒是变了。

zh: The book title stayed the same; the deadline changed. 😅
en: 如果预测有“延期通知”，这应该已经是经典案例。

zh: If predictions had extension notices, this would be a classic case. 📄
en: 2001→2011→2012。时间轴本身已经比预测更有戏剧性。

zh: 2001→2011→2012. The timeline itself became more dramatic than the prediction. 🎭
en: 预测未来最难的部分：未来真的会到来。

zh: The hardest part of predicting the future: the future eventually arrives. ⏰
en: 2011年，中国没有收到“请按预测崩溃”的通知。

zh: In 2011, China apparently never received the “please collapse as predicted” memo. 📩
en: 2001年的判断，到了2011年由本人确认“wrong”。

zh: By 2011, the 2001 prediction was acknowledged by Chang himself as “wrong.” ✔️
en: 但2011年底的文章又说：别以为我撤回预测。

zh: Yet his late-2011 article said: don't think I'm taking the prediction back. 🤔
en: 这就是预测界的“错了，但故事还没完”。

zh: That's the forecasting version of “wrong, but the story isn't over.” 📺
en: 如果现实没有配合，先调整日期，而不是调整叙事。

zh: When reality doesn't cooperate, the date can be adjusted before the narrative. 📅
en: 2001年的“十年”，最终变成了“十一年”。

zh: The “ten years” of 2001 eventually became “eleven years.” ➕1
en: 2011年的“错了”，紧接着是2012年的“再赌一次”。

zh: “Wrong in 2011” was followed by “bet on 2012.” 🎲
en: “Bet on it”这种语气，碰上现实就很有喜剧效果。

zh: “Bet on it” sounds rather different after reality answers back. 🎰
en: 2011年底公开写下“Bet on it”，然后历史继续向前走。

zh: He wrote “Bet on it” in late 2011. History kept moving. 🚶
en: 预测不是彩票，日期写得越具体，越容易被时间核对。

zh: Forecasts aren't lottery tickets; the more specific the date, the easier they are to fact-check. 🧐
en: 2001年的核心预测，现在最大的价值之一就是成为一个预测案例。

zh: One enduring value of the 2001 forecast is that it became a forecasting case study. 📖
en: 2006年的作者问答页面仍写着“within this decade—in other words, by 2011”。

zh: His Q&A page said: “within this decade—in other words, by 2011.” 📅
en: 这句话最不需要解释的部分，就是“by 2011”。

zh: The least ambiguous part of that sentence was “by 2011.” 😬
en: 2011来了，日期非常准；预测结果没有。

zh: 2011 arrived right on schedule. The predicted outcome didn't. ⏰
en: 时间管理满分，预测管理另说。

zh: Excellent calendar management; forecasting is another question. 📅
en: 如果把“崩溃”当成航班，它已经经历多次改签。

zh: If “collapse” were a flight, it has had several reschedulings. ✈️
en: 2001：预计十年。

zh: 2011：预计一年。
en: 这不是倒计时，这是滚动更新。

zh: 2001: ten years.
en: 2011: one more year.

zh: That's not a countdown; that's a rolling update. 🔄
en: 预测最大的魅力，就是多年以后还能拿出来核对。

zh: The great thing about predictions is that years later, you can still check them. 🔍
en: 2001年的预测经得起查档，因为原文还在那里。

zh: The 2001 prediction is easy to verify because the original record is still there. 📚
en: 最方便的事实核查方法：直接看当年的截止日期。

zh: The easiest fact-check: look at the deadline given at the time. 🔎
en: 不需要阴谋论，不需要剪辑，原始时间轴已经够精彩。

zh: No conspiracy theories or edits needed—the original timeline is entertaining enough. 😄
en: 2001年的判断不是“可能很久以后”，而是给出了具体期限。

zh: The 2001 prediction wasn't “sometime eventually”; it gave a specific timeframe. 📆
en: 所以今天回看，最值得看的不是情绪，而是日期。

zh: Looking back today, the most revealing thing isn't emotion. It's the date. 📅
en: 预测如果没有截止日期，很难核验；有了截止日期，就很容易核验。

zh: Predictions without deadlines are hard to test. Predictions with deadlines are easy. ✔️
en: 这一次，时间本身就是事实核查工具。

zh: This time, time itself is the fact-checking tool. ⏳
en: 2001年写下的期限，2011年自动进入历史记录。

zh: A deadline written in 2001 automatically became historical record in 2011. 📜
en: 历史最大的优点：不会因为你改口就自动修改旧档案。

zh: History's great feature: it doesn't automatically rewrite old records when you revise them. 📚
en: 截止日期到了，现实不会因为预测者很有信心就暂停。

zh: When the deadline arrives, reality doesn't pause because the forecaster is confident. 😅
en: “我非常确定”并不会改变日历。

zh: “I'm very certain” doesn't change the calendar. 📅
en: 预测未来之前，最好先确认未来有权拒绝你的剧本。

zh: Before predicting the future, remember that the future is allowed to reject your script. 🎬
en: 这类案例最适合提醒所有人：预测不是事实。

zh: Cases like this remind everyone: a prediction is not a fact. 🧠
en: 2009年，他仍认为中国政治体系会“fail soon”。

zh: In 2009, he still said China's political system would “fail soon.” 📉
en: “Soon”这个词比“2011”灵活多了。

zh: “Soon” is much more flexible than “2011.” 😅
en: 从具体日期到“soon”，时间表达越来越有弹性。

zh: From a specific date to “soon,” the timeframe became increasingly elastic. 🧘
2009：soon。
en: 语言学家可以研究一下这个时间单位。
2009: soon.

zh: Linguists may want to study this unit of time. 😂
en: “Soon”是预测世界的橡皮筋：拉多远都能解释。

zh: “Soon” is the rubber band of forecasting: stretch it far enough and it still fits. 🪢
en: 2012年CNN采访中，他承认2011年的预测错了。

zh: In a 2012 CNN interview, he acknowledged that the 2011 prediction was wrong.
en: 这条不用嘲讽，原始记录自己就够完整。

zh: No extra mockery needed; the original record speaks for itself. 📜
en: 真正值得转发的，是“本人承认错了”这部分。

zh: The most shareable part is simply the on-record admission that it was wrong. 🔍
en: 事实核查的高级玩法：让当事人自己的旧采访对照自己的旧预测。

zh: Advanced fact-checking: compare the person's own interview with their own prediction. 🔎
en: 最稳定的梗不是恶搞，而是原文时间轴。

zh: The most durable joke isn't parody; it's the original timeline. 📆
en: 2012年，他解释为什么2011年没有发生。

zh: In 2012, he explained why the 2011 event hadn't happened. 🎙️
en: 这意味着预测失败本身，也成为了新的解释对象。

zh: That means the failed prediction itself became the subject of a new explanation. 🔄
en: 预测→失误→解释→再次预测。

zh: Prediction → miss → explanation → another prediction. 🔁
en: 这条链条本身已经足够做成信息图。

zh: That sequence alone could be an infographic. 📊
en: “为什么没发生？”有解释；“那什么时候发生？”继续等。

zh: “Why didn't it happen?” got an explanation. “So when?” remained pending. ⏳
en: 预测失败后最重要的事情，是重新检查模型，而不是只换日期。

zh: After a forecast fails, the key question is whether the model needs revision—not merely the date. 🧮
en: 一个预测如果反复延长期限，就应该接受更多核验。

zh: A forecast repeatedly extended deserves more scrutiny. 🔍
en: 时间越长，原始预测越值得和现实逐项对照。

zh: The longer the timeline, the more useful the original forecast becomes for comparison. 📊
en: 这不是“谁更聪明”的问题，而是“当年到底说了什么”。

zh: This isn't about who's smarter; it's about what was actually said. 📜
en: 最好的吐槽往往只需要三个东西：原文、日期、现实。

zh: The best fact-check humor often needs only three things: the quote, the date, and reality. 📅
en: 2001年的书名非常大胆，时间表也非常具体。

zh: The 2001 book title was bold, and its timeline was specific. 📚
en: 标题负责吸引眼球，时间负责接受检验。

zh: The title grabs attention; the timeline gets tested. 👀
en: 书可以畅销，预测仍然需要接受现实检验。

zh: A book can sell well; its predictions still face reality. 📖
en: “畅销书”不是“已验证预测”的同义词。

zh: “Bestseller” is not a synonym for “validated forecast.” 📚≠✔️
en: 作者身份不是时间机器。

zh: Being an author doesn't make anyone a time machine. ⏰
en: 专家可以预测错，关键是历史会留下记录。

zh: Experts can be wrong; the key is that history keeps records. 📜
en: 预测者最难控制的变量：不可控的现实。

zh: The hardest variable for a forecaster to control: reality. 🌍
en: 2001年如果有“提醒我十年后检查结果”，今天应该已经响了。

zh: If 2001 had a “remind me in ten years” button, it would've gone off long ago. 🔔
en: 可惜历史没有“忽略通知”按钮。

zh: Unfortunately, history has no “ignore notification” button. 🔔😂
en: 预测可以大胆，但核验必须冷静。

zh: Predictions can be bold; verification should be calm. 🧊
en: 2012年文章的标题甚至直接用了“2012 Edition”。

zh: His 2012 article was literally titled “2012 Edition.” 📚
en: 这名字的喜剧感来自它确实发生在2011年底。

zh: The humor comes from the fact that it was actually published at the end of 2011. 😅
en: 2011没等来结局，2012版及时上线。

zh: 2011 didn't deliver the finale; the 2012 edition arrived on schedule. 🎬
en: 如果预测是软件，这叫“版本更新”。

zh: If forecasting were software, this would be a version update. 💻
en: Version 2011 failed to launch. Version 2012 followed.

zh: 2011版本未按计划上线，2012版本紧随其后。😂
en: 现实：服务器正常运行。

zh: 预测：正在重试……
en: Reality: server operating normally.

zh: Forecast: retrying… 🔄
en: “Collapse.exe”在2011年没有成功启动。

zh: “Collapse.exe” failed to launch in 2011. 💻
en: 2012年又尝试启动一次。

zh: It tried launching again in 2012. 😂
en: 预测界面的“预计完成时间”似乎需要手动刷新。

zh: The forecast dashboard's “estimated completion time” seems to require manual refresh. 🔄
en: 这不是金融软件，为什么总有“延期交付”？

zh: This isn't a software project—why are there so many deadline extensions? 😭
en: 如果预测有GitHub，commit history一定很精彩。

zh: If forecasts had GitHub, the commit history would be fascinating. 🧑‍💻
en: collapse_2011 → collapse_2012 → collapse_soon。

zh: collapse_2011 → collapse_2012 → collapse_soon. 😂
en: 版本号越来越新，原始预测越来越值得考古。

zh: The version number gets newer; the original prediction becomes more archaeological. 🏺
en: 最经典的bug不是“预测错”，而是“预测日期错”。

zh: The classic bug isn't merely the prediction being wrong; it's the deadline being wrong. 🐛
en: 日历不会因为软件更新而回到2001年。

zh: A software update can't reset the calendar to 2001. 📅
en: 历史记录：不可覆盖。

zh: History log: read-only. 🔒
en: 预测记录：可以解释。

zh: Prediction record: open to interpretation. 📝
en: 两者放一起看，信息量就出来了。

zh: Put the two together, and the contrast speaks for itself. 🔎
en: 最好的“打脸”不是编段子，是打开原始档案。

zh: The best fact-check isn't a made-up joke; it's opening the original archive. 📂
en: 2001年的原文，比2026年的二手梗更有杀伤力。

zh: The 2001 original is more powerful than any 2026 meme. 📚
en: 2002年他对台湾听众说，中国政府会在“五六年、最多十年”内崩溃。

zh: In 2002, he told a Taiwanese audience the Chinese government would collapse in five or six years, ten at most.
en: “五六年，最多十年”——这个时间窗口如今已经全部进入历史。

zh: “Five or six years, ten at most”—that entire window is now history. ⏳
en: 这次连“十年”都不是模糊表达，而是公开记录里的具体说法。

zh: Here, even “ten years” was a specific statement on the public record. 📜
en: 2002年的十年上限，对应2012年。

zh: The ten-year maximum from 2002 points to 2012. 📅
en: 而2012年已经过去很多年了。

zh: And 2012 has been gone for many years. 😶
en: 时间轴这种东西，最大的特点是不会倒着走。

zh: One feature of timelines: they don't run backward. ⏰
en: 2002：最多十年。

zh: 2012：十年到期。
en: 现实：继续运行。

zh: 2002: ten years at most.
en: 2012: deadline reached.

zh: Reality: continued operating. 😅
en: “最多十年”是一种非常适合被历史核查的句式。

zh: “Ten years at most” is a phrase history can verify very easily. 🔍
en: 如果一句预测有明确上限，它就天然拥有一个核验日期。

zh: A prediction with a clear upper limit naturally has a verification date. 📆
en: 这个日期已经过去了。

zh: That date has passed. ⏳
en: 2002年的听众不需要等新闻推送，直接看日历就能知道结果。

zh: The 2002 audience doesn't need a news alert—just check the calendar. 📅
en: 这就是为什么老预测特别适合做事实核查。

zh: That's why old predictions are perfect for fact-checking. 🔎
en: “十年内”听起来很长，历史一眨眼就过去。

zh: “Within ten years” sounds long; history makes it disappear quickly. ⏱️
en: 2002年的倒计时已经结束，核验环节还在继续。

zh: The 2002 countdown is over; the verification continues. 🔍
en: 预测者给了时间窗口，历史给了最终答案。

zh: The forecaster gave a window; history supplied the result. 📜
en: 最有意思的不是预测很大胆，而是它真的留下了明确日期。

zh: What's most interesting isn't that it was bold, but that it left a clear date. 📅
en: 不需要“我听说”，因为当年的媒体报道就在。

zh: No “I heard”; the contemporary reporting is there. 📰
en: 不需要截图考古到天荒地老，原始报道已经记录。

zh: No endless screenshot archaeology; contemporary reports recorded it. 🗃️
en: 事实核查的快乐：原始材料自己会说话。

zh: The joy of fact-checking: primary records speak for themselves. 📜
en: 当年的预测越具体，今天越容易核对。

zh: The more specific the prediction, the easier it is to check today. 🔍
en: 2001年的书曾把WTO入世与中国政治经济压力联系起来。

zh: The 2001 book linked WTO accession with political and economic pressure on China.
en: 结果是：WTO入世发生了，预测中的时间表没有照着走。

zh: WTO accession happened; the predicted timeline did not follow. 📆
en: 这提醒我们：相关性≠必然结果。

zh: It reminds us: correlation does not guarantee the predicted outcome. 🧠
en: 国际事件可以成为变量，但变量不是剧本。

zh: International events can be variables, not scripts. 🌍
en: 预测最容易犯的错误之一，就是把一个变量写成必然结局。

zh: One forecasting error is treating a variable as a guaranteed ending. 📊
en: WTO入世不是“自动触发崩溃”的按钮。

zh: WTO accession was not an automatic “collapse” button. 🔘
en: 历史不是多米诺骨牌游戏，每块牌都不会按预设方向倒。

zh: History isn't a domino game where every piece must fall as predicted. 🁢
en: 一个经济事件可以产生很多结果，不只有一种终局。

zh: One economic event can produce many outcomes, not one predetermined ending. 🔀
en: 这就是为什么预测需要不断接受现实检验。

zh: That's why forecasts need continuous reality checks. 🔍
en: 当年的核心变量值得研究，最终预测同样值得核查。

zh: The variables were worth studying; the final prediction is worth checking too. 📊
en: 2009年他把中国经济描述为出口依赖，并预期刺激政策会带来长期问题。

zh: In 2009 he described China as export-dependent and argued stimulus would create longer-term problems.
en: 这是一个可以讨论的经济判断，但它不能自动证明政治崩溃日期。

zh: That's a debatable economic assessment; it doesn't automatically prove a political-collapse date. 📊
en: 经济预测和政治预测不是同一个方程。

zh: Economic forecasting and political forecasting aren't the same equation. ➗
en: GDP、债务、贸易和政治稳定之间存在复杂关系。

zh: GDP, debt, trade and political stability have complex relationships. 🧮
en: “存在风险”与“将在某年崩溃”是两种完全不同的表述。

zh: “There is risk” and “it will collapse in a certain year” are very different claims. ⚖️
en: 前者需要分析，后者需要时间来验。

zh: The former needs analysis; the latter needs a date to test. 📅
en: 时间到了以后，第二种说法就可以被直接核对。

zh: Once the date passes, the second claim can be directly tested. 🔍
en: 所以具体日期既增加了冲击力，也增加了可证伪性。

zh: Specific dates increase impact—and falsifiability. 🎯
en: 这就是为什么“2011”“2012”特别适合被反复引用。

zh: That's why “2011” and “2012” remain especially easy to fact-check. 📆
en: 一个日期，胜过一百个模糊形容词。

zh: One date can be more informative than a hundred vague adjectives. 📅
en: 2012年CNN采访中，他解释自己为什么没有在2011年预测成功。

zh: In a 2012 CNN interview, he explained why his 2011 prediction failed.
en: 这其实是最标准的预测复盘材料。

zh: That's actually classic forecast-review material. 📊
en: 预测失败之后解释原因，本身没有问题。

zh: Explaining a failed forecast is not inherently a problem. 🧠
en: 真正值得关注的是：原来的结论是否因此得到修正。

zh: The key question is whether the original conclusion gets revised. 🔎
en: 预测学最需要的不是自信，而是校准。

zh: Forecasting needs calibration, not just confidence. 🎯
en: 如果现实不断偏离预测，模型就值得重新检查。

zh: If reality repeatedly diverges from a forecast, the model deserves re-examination. 📈
en: 这条原则适用于所有预测者，不只适用于一个人。

zh: That principle applies to all forecasters, not just one person. 🌍
en: 所以拿旧预测出来核对，并不是针对个人，而是检查预测方法。

zh: Checking old forecasts isn't merely personal; it's a test of forecasting methods. 🔬
en: 最好的“吐槽”可以同时是一堂预测学公开课。

zh: The best satire can also be a public lesson in forecasting. 🎓
en: 预测不是信仰，应该允许现实打分——只是不要替现实提前写答案。

zh: Forecasting isn't faith; reality gets the final check. Don't write the answer in advance. 🧠
en: 2012年他仍认为中国政治体系存在根本性问题。

zh: In 2012 he still argued that China's political system faced fundamental problems.
en: “存在问题”与“某年必然崩溃”之间，有一整条逻辑链。

zh: Between “there are problems” and “collapse must happen by year X” lies an entire chain of reasoning. 🔗
en: 问题可以真实存在，预测时间仍然可能错误。

zh: Problems can be real while the predicted timing is still wrong. 🧩
en: 这是讨论政治预测时非常重要的区别。

zh: That's an important distinction in political forecasting. ⚖️
en: 预测错日期，不等于所有风险分析都自动归零。

zh: Getting the date wrong doesn't automatically invalidate every risk assessment. 📊
en: 反过来也一样：指出风险存在，也不等于崩溃日期就正确。

zh: Conversely, identifying risks doesn't make a collapse date correct. 🔄
en: 最严谨的吐槽，应该把两件事分开。

zh: The most rigorous satire keeps those two things separate. 🧠
en: 可以吐槽预测失准，但别替历史添加不存在的原话。

zh: You can mock an inaccurate forecast without inventing quotations. 🚫📝
en: 可以引用公开记录，但最好保留上下文。

zh: Public records are fair game, but context matters. 📚
en: “他说过什么”和“后来发生什么”最好分成两栏。

zh: Put “what he said” and “what happened later” in separate columns. 📊

en: 2012年：再预测。

zh: 2026年：继续核验。
en: 2001: prediction.

zh: 2011: verification.
en: 2012: another prediction.

zh: 2026: still verifying. 😂
en: 这条时间线比任何P图都更有效。

zh: This timeline is more effective than any Photoshop job. 🖼️
en: 不需要给他P脸，给时间轴P出来就够了。

zh: No need to Photoshop his face; the timeline does the work. 😅
en: 不需要造梗，梗已经写进历史记录。

zh: No need to manufacture the meme; the meme is already in the record. 📜
en: 最强的素材不是传闻，是他自己公开发表的预测。

zh: The strongest material isn't rumor; it's his own public forecasts. 🎙️
en: 这叫“自带素材库”。

zh: That's what you call a built-in archive. 📚
en: 2001年的一句预测，足够互联网复读很多年。

zh: One 2001 prediction can fuel years of internet fact-checking. 🔁
en: 但复读时最好附原始出处。

zh: But when reposting, attach the original source. 🔗
en: 因为截图可以断章取义，原文可以让大家自己判断。

zh: Screenshots can lose context; originals let people judge for themselves. 🔍
en: 这才是X平台真正耐用的“社区注释”。

zh: That's the kind of community note that actually lasts on X. 📝
en: 2001年的预测已经成为历史材料，而不是未来消息。

zh: The 2001 prediction is now historical material, not breaking news. 📰➡️📚
en: “即将发生”经过二十多年后，已经需要重新定义“即将”。

zh: After more than two decades, “coming” may need a dictionary entry. 📖😂
en: 如果“soon”可以无限延长，它就失去了时间预测的功能。

zh: If “soon” can stretch indefinitely, it loses its forecasting value. ⏳
en: 具体日期之所以重要，就是因为它不能无限拉伸。

zh: Specific dates matter because they can't stretch indefinitely. 📅
en: 这就是为什么2011和2012如此好用。

zh: That's why 2011 and 2012 are so useful for fact-checking. 🔎
en: 预测历史的第一课：保存原文。

zh: First lesson of forecasting history: save the original. 📂
en: 第二课：保存日期。

zh: Second lesson: save the date. 📅
en: 第三课：等时间过去。

zh: Third lesson: let time pass. ⏳
en: 第四课：回来核对。

zh: Fourth lesson: come back and check. 🔍
en: 第五课：不要因为标题很震撼，就跳过验证。

zh: Fifth lesson: don't skip verification because the headline is dramatic. 🧠
en: “中国即将崩溃”是一个非常强烈的命题，所以自然需要非常强的证据。

zh: “China is about to collapse” is a very strong claim, so it requires very strong evidence. ⚖️
en: 强烈预测不是免检产品。

zh: Strong predictions aren't exempt from fact-checking. 🔍
en: 专家身份也不是免检产品。

zh: Expert status isn't an exemption from fact-checking either. 🎓
en: 畅销书也不是免检产品。

zh: Bestseller status isn't an exemption either. 📚
en: 媒体曝光更不是免检产品。

zh: Media exposure isn't an exemption either. 📺
en: 唯一真正的免检对象？不存在。

zh: The only truly exempt thing? Nothing. 😅
en: 现实可以让任何预测重新接受考试。

zh: Reality can put any prediction back on the exam. 📝
en: 预测者可以有观点，历史仍然有时间轴。

zh: Forecasters can have opinions; history still has a timeline. ⏰
en: 观点可以争论，日期可以核验。

zh: Opinions can be debated; dates can be checked. 🔎
en: 所以最硬核的吐槽方式：少骂人，多放原始出处。

zh: The most rigorous roast: fewer insults, more primary sources. 📚🔥
en: “2011”——一个值得永远出现在章家敦相关事实核查里的数字。

zh: “2011” — a number that deserves a permanent place in fact-checking about Chang. 📅
en: “2012”——因为上一站没有按时到达，所以出现的下一站。

zh: “2012” — the next stop after the previous one failed to arrive on time. 🚉😂
en: “Soon”——预测界最耐用的时间单位之一。

zh: “Soon” — one of forecasting's most durable units of time. ⏳
en: “Collapse”——标题里很短，现实里很复杂。

zh: “Collapse” — short in a headline, complicated in reality. 🧩
en: “Prediction”——最适合多年后重新阅读的文学体裁。

zh: “Prediction” — perhaps the genre most worth rereading years later. 📖
en: 2001年的预测可以被重新阅读；2026年的读者也可以自己判断。

zh: The 2001 forecast can be reread, and 2026 readers can judge for themselves. 🔎
en: 最有意思的不是“他到底是不是预言家”，而是把原话、日期和结果摆在一起。

zh: The interesting part isn't whether he's a “prophet”; it's putting the words, dates, and outcomes side by side. 📊
en: 真正经得起传播的内容，不需要伪造“名言”。

zh: Content worth sharing doesn't need fabricated “quotes.” 🚫
en: 章家敦的预测史，本身就是一个很好的“如何核验专家预测”的案例。

zh: Gordon Chang's forecasting record itself is a useful case study in how to evaluate expert predictions. 🔍
en: 最后一条：别替他说没说过的话；把他真正说过的、真正写过的、真正标过日期的内容摆出来——剩下的，让时间自己说。
